mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-p1.title: Estimate
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-p1.body:
$11^2$ is a bit more than $10^2 = 100$, so the answer is a bit more than 100. Only 123 fits.

**Answer: (C) 123**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-p2.title: Twenty coins make £1
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-p2.body:
Twenty 5p coins make £1. $2020 \div 20 = 101$, so she has £101.

**Answer: (C) £101**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-01.title: Convert first
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-01.body:
When it is 3 p.m. in Singapore, it is 7 hours earlier in Manchester: 8 a.m. Add the 15-hour flight: 8 a.m. + 15 hours = 11 p.m. Manchester time.

**Answer: (D) 11 p.m.**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-01.title: Fly first, then convert
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-01.body:
3 p.m. + 15 hours = 6 a.m. the next day, Singapore time. Manchester is 7 hours behind, so it is 11 p.m. there.

**Answer: (D) 11 p.m.**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-02.title: What's left
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-02.body:
Cutting 1 cm from each edge leaves an $8 \times 8$ cm square: 64 cm². The toast was $10 \times 10 = 100$ cm², so $100 - 64 = 36$ cm² is thrown away, which is $\frac{36}{100} = 36\%$.

**Answer: (E) 36%**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-02.title: Count the crust strips
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-02.body:
Top and bottom strips: $10 \times 1$ each, so 20 cm². Left and right strips (between them): $8 \times 1$ each, so 16 cm². Total 36 cm² out of 100 cm²: 36%. (Watch out: $4 \times 10 = 40$ counts the corners twice.)

**Answer: (E) 36%**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-03.title: Last digit
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-03.body:
The last digit of $3333 \times 4444$ is the last digit of $3 \times 4 = 12$, which is 2. Only 14 811 852 ends in 2.

**Answer: (C) 14 811 852**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-04.title: Match them up
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-04.body:
Pair each odd number with the even number one bigger: 1 with 2, 3 with 4, ..., 99 with 100. There are 50 pairs, and each even number is 1 more, so Steven's total is $2500 + 50 = 2550$.

**Answer: (D) 2550**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-05.title: Square plus triangles
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-05.body:
The square is $3 \times 3 = 9$ cm². Each triangle has base 3 cm and height 5 cm, so its area is $\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 5 = 7.5$ cm². The star is $9 + 4 \times 7.5 = 9 + 30 = 39$ cm².

**Answer: (E) 39 cm²**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-05.title: Pair the triangles
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-05.body:
Two triangles together make a $3 \times 5$ rectangle (15 cm²), so the four triangles make 30 cm². Add the 9 cm² square: 39 cm².

**Answer: (E) 39 cm²**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-06.title: Sock-days
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-06.body:
80 socks make 40 pairs. Each pair lasts 100 days, so altogether he has $40 \times 100 = 4000$ days of wear. A year is about 365 days, and $10 \times 365 = 3650 < 4000$, so it is more than 10 years.

**Answer: (E) more than 10**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-06.title: Each sock separately
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-06.body:
He wears 2 socks a day, so in a year he uses about $2 \times 365 = 730$ sock-days. The 80 socks give $80 \times 100 = 8000$ sock-days. $8000 \div 730 \approx 11$ years.

**Answer: (E) more than 10**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-07.title: Count the overlap
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-07.body:
$28 - 13 = 15$ pupils like at least one of them. But $8 + 10 = 18$, which is 3 more than 15, so 3 pupils were counted twice — they like both.

**Answer: (A) 3**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-07.title: Venn diagram
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-07.body:
With 3 in the middle: cabbage only $8 - 3 = 5$, sprouts only $10 - 3 = 7$, neither 13. Total $5 + 3 + 7 + 13 = 28$ ✓.

**Answer: (A) 3**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-08.title: List them
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-08.body:
Call the dogs A to F. Pairs with A: AB, AC, AD, AE, AF (5). New pairs with B: BC, BD, BE, BF (4). Then C: 3, D: 2, E: 1. Total $5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 15$.

**Answer: (D) 15**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-08.title: Choose and halve
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-08.body:
The first dog can be any of 6, the second any of the other 5: $6 \times 5 = 30$. But each pair was counted twice (AB and BA), so there are $30 \div 2 = 15$ pairs.

**Answer: (D) 15**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-09.title: Convert to minutes
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-09.body:
13 hours is $13 \times 60 = 780$ minutes. Shared over 60 rides: $780 \div 60 = 13$ minutes per ride.

**Answer: (A) 13 minutes**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-09.title: Neat shortcut
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-09.body:
60 rides and 60 minutes in an hour: each hour of riding gives 1 minute per ride. 13 hours gives 13 minutes per ride.

**Answer: (A) 13 minutes**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-10.title: Compare the pictures
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-10.body:
Table + 3 bricks $= 150$ cm and table + 1 brick $= 140$ cm. The difference, 2 bricks, is 10 cm, so one brick is 5 cm. The table is $140 - 5 = 135$ cm.

**Answer: (E) 135 cm**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-10.title: Test the options
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-10.body:
If the table is 135 cm, the brick is $140 - 135 = 5$ cm, and three bricks are 15 cm: $135 + 15 = 150$ ✓.

**Answer: (E) 135 cm**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-11.title: Even tens digit
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-11.body:
After doubling, the answer is even, so its last digit is even. Reversed, that last digit becomes the first digit of my number. So my number has an even tens digit: only 26 or 48. 48 gives 106, which has 3 digits. 26 works: $(26 + 5) \times 2 = 62$.

**Answer: (B) 26**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-12.title: Fire engine + motorcycle pairs
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-12.body:
Each fire engine comes with a motorcycle, worth $9 + 2 = 11$ points together. So 63 minus the bus points must be a multiple of 11. Try the numbers of buses: 3 buses leave 48, 4 leave 43, 5 leave 38, 6 leave 33 $= 3 \times 11$ ✓, 7 leave 28. So he sees 6 buses (and 3 fire engines and 3 motorcycles).

**Answer: (D) 6**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-12.title: Start from the pairs
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-12.body:
The pairs give 11, 22, 33, 44 or 55 points. The rest, $63 - 11 = 52$, $41$, $30$, $19$, $8$, must be a multiple of 5 for the buses. Only 30 works: $30 \div 5 = 6$ buses.

**Answer: (D) 6**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-13.title: Use odd and even
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-13.body:
The three primes add to $3 \times 8 = 24$, an even number. Three odd numbers would add to an odd number, so one of them must be 2 (the only even prime). The other two add to 22: $3 + 19$, $5 + 17$ or $11 + 11$. The two smaller primes are then 2 and 3 (difference 1, not prime), 2 and 5 (difference 3, prime ✓), or 2 and 11 (difference 9 ✗). So the primes are 2, 5, 17.

**Answer: (D) 17**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-14.title: Check the options
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-14.body:
The number must be 6 more than a square number and 11 less than another square number.
- 31: $31 - 6 = 25$ ✓, $31 + 11 = 42$ ✗
- 38: 32 ✗
- 42: 36 ✓, 53 ✗
- 55: 49 ✓, 66 ✗
- 70: 64 ✓, 81 ✓

**Answer: (E) 70**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-14.title: Squares 17 apart
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-14.body:
The two squares differ by $6 + 11 = 17$. Square numbers 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, ...: the gaps between neighbours are 3, 5, 7, ..., 17 — the gap between 64 and 81. So he has $64 + 6 = 70$ cabbages.

**Answer: (E) 70**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-15.title: Fractions of the square
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-15.body:
The square has area $12 \times 12 = 144$ cm². In a tangram, a diagonal cuts the square in half, and each big triangle is a quarter of the square. The parallelogram is made of two small triangles, each a quarter of a big triangle: so each small triangle is $\frac{1}{16}$ of the square and the parallelogram is $\frac{2}{16} = \frac{1}{8}$ of it. $\frac{1}{8} \times 144 = 18$ cm².

**Answer: (B) 18**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-15.title: Base and height
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-15.body:
The tick marks divide the left side into quarters of 3 cm. The parallelogram's vertical sides are each 6 cm long and they are 3 cm apart horizontally (a quarter of the square's width). Area $= 6 \times 3 = 18$ cm².

**Answer: (B) 18**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-16.title: Machine-days
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-16.body:
The crop needs $4 \times 6 = 24$ machine-days of work. With 3 machines: $24 \div 3 = 8$ days.

**Answer: (B) 8 days**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-16.title: Fewer machines, more time
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-16.body:
1 machine would take 4 times as long: 24 days. 3 machines take a third of that: 8 days.

**Answer: (B) 8 days**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-17.title: Use the diameter
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-17.body:
Each coin is $2 \times 3 = 6$ cm across. $4000 \times 6 = 24\,000$ cm. 100 cm make 1 m, so this is 240 m.

**Answer: (C) 240 m**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-17.title: Coins per metre
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-17.body:
About $100 \div 6 \approx 16.7$ coins fit in a metre, so 4000 coins need about $4000 \div 16.7 \approx 240$ m.

**Answer: (C) 240 m**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-18.title: Check the options
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-18.body:
Look for a pair of neighbouring digits that is not a multiple of 3:
- B: 637 542 has 37 ✗
- C: 721 543 has 43 ✗
- D: 751 263 has 26 ✗
- E: 7 563 421 has 56 ✗
- A: 75 421 has 75, 54, 42, 21 — all multiples of 3 ✓

**Answer: (A) 75 421**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-18.title: Build the largest
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-18.body:
A two-digit number is a multiple of 3 when its digit sum is. 3 and 6 can only pair with each other, so they can't both be used in a long chain with the others; use 1, 2, 4, 5, 7. Start with the biggest digit, 7. Next must make a multiple of 3: 75. Then 54, then 42, then 21. This uses all five digits: 75 421, and no longer number is possible.

**Answer: (A) 75 421**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-19.title: Count corners
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-19.body:
Each end of the cut either goes through a corner of the octagon or through the middle of a side.
- Through two corners: the 8 corners are shared out, with the two cut corners in both pieces: total $8 + 2 = 10$ corners (e.g. 5 + 5, 4 + 6).
- Through a corner and a side: total $8 + 1 + 2 = 11$ (e.g. 5 + 6).
- Through two sides: total $8 + 4 = 12$ (e.g. 6 + 6, 3 + 9).

A triangle and a hexagon would have $3 + 6 = 9$ corners — impossible. (Cutting off a triangle leaves a heptagon, octagon or nonagon.)

**Answer: (A) 1 triangle and 1 hexagon**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-20.title: Each edge touches two faces
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-20.body:
There are 6 faces and each edge belongs to exactly 2 faces, so 2 red edges can cover at most 4 faces. At least 3 red edges are needed. 3 is enough: choose three edges that don't share any face, e.g. on a cube with top/bottom, front/back, left/right: the top-front edge, the bottom-left edge and the back-right (vertical) edge. These touch top+front, bottom+left, back+right — all six faces.

**Answer: (B) 3**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-21.title: Add the angles at P
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-21.body:
The interior angles are: pentagon $180° - 360° \div 5 = 108°$, hexagon $180° - 60° = 120°$, octagon $180° - 45° = 135°$. Around $P$ they add to $108° + 120° + 135° = 363°$, which is $3°$ more than a full turn. So the pentagon and hexagon overlap by $3°$.

**Answer: (C) 3°**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-22.title: Use the same ratio
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-22.body:
The rectangles with areas 4 and 5 have the same width, so the bottom row is $\frac{5}{4}$ times as tall as the top row. The missing rectangle $MOLS$ has the same width as $PJOM$ and is $\frac{5}{4}$ times as tall, so its area is $3 \times \frac{5}{4} = 3.75$ cm². Total $3 + 4 + 5 + 3.75 = 15.75$ cm².

**Answer: (C) 15.75**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-22.title: Cross-multiply
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-22.body:
In a rectangle cut into four by two lines, opposite pieces have equal products: (top-left) × (bottom-right) = (top-right) × (bottom-left). So bottom-left $= 3 \times 5 \div 4 = 3.75$, and the total is 15.75.

**Answer: (C) 15.75**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-23.title: Use 100 ml
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-23.body:
Say each jar starts with 100 ml.
- Pour half of X into Y: X has 50 ml blackcurrant; Y has 100 ml orange + 50 ml blackcurrant.
- Pour half of Y into X: that is 50 ml orange + 25 ml blackcurrant.

X now has $50 + 25 = 75$ ml blackcurrant and 50 ml orange: $75 : 50 = 3 : 2$.

**Answer: (D) 3 : 2**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-23.title: Use fractions
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-23.body:
Call the starting amount 1. X keeps $\frac{1}{2}$ blackcurrant. Y gets $\frac{1}{2}$ blackcurrant and has 1 orange; half of Y is $\frac{1}{4}$ blackcurrant and $\frac{1}{2}$ orange. X ends with $\frac{3}{4}$ blackcurrant and $\frac{1}{2}$ orange, i.e. $3 : 2$.

**Answer: (D) 3 : 2**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-24.title: The inner block
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-24.body:
$125 = 5 \times 5 \times 5$, so the cubes form a $5 \times 5 \times 5$ block. Remove the cubes touching the four sides: that leaves a $3 \times 3$ column. Remove the bottom layer, which touches the base: $3 \times 3 \times 4 = 36$ cubes remain. The top layer is not removed since there is no lid.

**Answer: (B) 36**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-24.title: Layer by layer
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-24.body:
Each of the 5 layers has a $3 \times 3 = 9$ middle part away from the sides. The bottom layer touches the base, so only the top 4 layers count: $4 \times 9 = 36$.

**Answer: (B) 36**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-25.title: Follow the cuts
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-25.body:
Each cut removes the biggest square possible:
- 297 × 210 → square 210, leaves 87 × 210
- 210 × 87 → squares 87, 87, leaves 36 × 87
- 87 × 36 → squares 36, 36, leaves 15 × 36
- 36 × 15 → squares 15, 15, leaves 6 × 15
- 15 × 6 → squares 6, 6, leaves 3 × 6
- 6 × 3 → two 3 × 3 squares.

**Answer: (C) 3 mm**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-25.title: Common factor
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2020-25.body:
Every cut keeps lengths that are differences of earlier lengths, so the final square side must divide both 210 and 297 — and in fact it is their highest common factor. $210 = 2 \times 3 \times 5 \times 7$ and $297 = 3^3 \times 11$, so the HCF is 3.

**Answer: (C) 3 mm**
